task.description:
WF-03 Step 1 (root-cause diagnosis) for ISS-0119. Produce a diagnosis CODE-DESIGNER can design a fix from. You do NOT implement the fix.

REPRODUCE FIRST -- do not diagnose from the bug report's prose (No Speculation). Concretely: measure the current byte size and line/entry count of docs/status/requirement_status.yaml yourself and quote the real numbers; then DEMONSTRATE the read limit is actually hit rather than asserting it (attempt a whole-file Read call and quote verbatim what came back). If the limit turns out NOT to be hit -- the number in the issue is stale, or the tool behaves differently than described -- say so plainly. That is a legitimate finding and it changes the shape of this whole run.

THEN establish each of the following, with evidence:

1. THE MECHANISM THAT BROKE. The safeguard's chain is 'read the file in full -> therefore notice the established schema -> therefore append rather than invent'. Name precisely which link the size now breaks, and state what an agent following today's written instructions literally would actually end up doing.

2. THE CONTRADICTION. core-directives.md's 'Load Scoped Context, Not Whole Files' pushes toward targeted reads of large files; the anti-patterns entry 'Overwriting docs/status/requirement_status.yaml instead of appending' and the file's own header comment push toward a full read. Quote both sides, and state exactly where an agent is left with no rule that resolves them for this one file.

3. THE BLAST RADIUS OF A SPLIT. Enumerate every place in the repo that references this file by path, and classify each as (i) prose mention only, (ii) an instruction telling an agent to read or append to it, or (iii) machine-parsed by code or a mix task. ORCH's own scan found roughly 13 doc referrers plus a mention at mix.exs line 50 and several docs/requirements.yaml entries that cite specific historical entries by REQ id -- RE-DERIVE this list yourself, do not inherit ORCH's count. This is what determines whether a split is cheap or expensive, and CODE-DESIGNER needs the real list.

4. THE SECOND GAP. Confirm or refute ISS-0119's claim that 'req: SCOPE-CHANGE' is the established convention for work not tied to a requirement, and that it is documented nowhere. Give the actual count of precedent entries. State whether any 'req: ISS-NNNN' entry exists anywhere in the file. State what the header currently does and does not say about the 'req' field.

5. WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE. State the constraints any fix is bound by -- in particular that ISS-0119 explicitly forbids resolving this by relaxing the append-only rule, and that this file is audit trail so a split may drop nothing. Do NOT choose between remedy (a) (split the file) and remedy (b) (rewrite the header to prescribe an executable safeguard). Present what each would have to satisfy and let CODE-DESIGNER decide. Naming trade-offs is in scope; making the design decision is not.

If you discover an unrelated defect while doing this, report it to ORCH in result.issues per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- do not call gh or letflow-queue yourself, and do not extend this run to fix it.
acceptance_criteria: The file's real current byte size, line count and entry count are measured and quoted, not taken from ISS-0119's prose
The read-limit failure is demonstrated with actual verbatim tool output, not asserted
The broken link of the read-in-full -> notice-schema -> append chain is named precisely
The core-directives vs anti-patterns contradiction is quoted from both sources, with the unresolved gap stated
Every referrer of docs/status/requirement_status.yaml is enumerated and classified prose-only / instruction / machine-parsed
The req: SCOPE-CHANGE convention claim is confirmed or refuted with a real count, and the presence or absence of any req: ISS-NNNN precedent is stated
Constraints on any fix are stated, including the explicit prohibition on relaxing the append-only rule and the no-history-may-be-dropped constraint
No fix is implemented and no remedy is chosen between (a) and (b)
No file outside this handoff is modified

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 1 root-cause diagnosis for ISS-0119. REPRODUCED. The defect is real and currently active. No fix implemented; no choice made between remedy (a) and remedy (b).

=== 0. REPRODUCTION (measured, not taken from the issue's prose) ===

MEASURED NOW (2026-08-21T04:51:34Z, working tree, branch feature/WF03-ISS0119-20260821):
  wc -c docs/status/requirement_status.yaml -> 361376 bytes
  wc -l                                     -> 5766 lines
  grep -c '^  - req: '                      -> 182 entries
  CR count (grep -c for carriage return)    -> 5766  (file is CRLF; git blob is 355610 LF bytes, working tree adds one CR per line = 361376)

READ-LIMIT FAILURE DEMONSTRATED, verbatim tool output from a Read call on the absolute path with no offset/limit:
  <error>File content (352.9KB) exceeds maximum allowed size (256KB). Use offset and limit parameters to read specific portions of the file, or search for specific content instead of reading the whole file.</error>
  (352.9KB = 361376/1024. The tool measures the CRLF working-tree bytes.)

A SCOPED read on the same file succeeds -- Read with offset=5755, limit=12 returned lines 5755-5766 normally. So the file is not corrupt or unreadable; only the whole-file read is refused.

ARE ISS-0119'S NUMBERS STALE? Partly, and in a way that does NOT weaken the issue. Byte count (361,376) and entry count (182) are exact and current. Line count is one entry stale: the issue says "~5,723 lines"; the real figure is 5,766. Cause established from git, not guessed: the file's last-touching commit c1f5e5c (2026-08-21) appended DOC-UPDATER's own entry -- git show c1f5e5c~1 gives 5723 lines / 181 entries / 30 SCOPE-CHANGE, git show c1f5e5c gives 5766 / 182 / 31. The issue text mixes post-append byte/entry figures with pre-append line/precedent figures. Immaterial: the limit is hit either way.

ADDITIONAL HARD DATUM ORCH DID NOT HAVE -- HOW LONG THE SAFEGUARD HAS BEEN DISARMED. I walked every commit that touched the file (git log --reverse, reconstructing working-tree size as blob bytes + line count for CRLF). The file first exceeded 262,144 bytes at commit 3d19e8c, "feat: drop tenant_id from ten schema-isolated business tables", 2026-08-18 20:32:52 +0500 = 2026-08-18T15:32:52Z, at 4,217 lines / 264,861 working-tree bytes. The prior commit (3a3b236, 2026-08-17) was 3,786 lines / 234,147 bytes -- comfortably readable. So the "read the file in full" instruction has been literally unexecutable for approximately 2.5 days and across every run merged since 2026-08-18, not since today. Every DOC-UPDATER turn in that window either improvised a substitute or believed it complied while seeing a fragment.

=== 1. THE MECHANISM THAT BROKE ===

The safeguard's chain is: [L1] read the file in full -> [L2] therefore notice the established schema -> [L3] therefore append rather than invent.

L1 IS THE BROKEN LINK, and it fails HARD (a refusal, not a truncation). That distinction is the whole diagnosis. A silent truncation would leave the agent with a fragment it believed was whole; a refusal leaves the agent with NOTHING and forces an improvised substitute. The tool's own error text then steers the improvisation: "Use offset and limit parameters to read specific portions of the file, or search for specific content instead of reading the whole file." So the failure path actively recommends the fragment read.

WHAT AN AGENT FOLLOWING TODAY'S WRITTEN INSTRUCTIONS LITERALLY WOULD ACTUALLY DO: doc-updater.md tells it to read the file "**in full**" and states "a full read is genuinely required here." It issues that read. It gets the refusal above. At that point NO written rule in this repo tells it what to do next -- not doc-updater.md, not core-directives.md, not WF-02, not the file's own header. It must invent a substitute unaided, and every available substitute is a window whose representativeness it cannot verify:
  - a head read (offset 0, limit 2000) covers 2000/5766 = 34.7% of the file and DOES include the header and the documented entry shape -- this is the benign case, and it is why the damage has been latent rather than immediate;
  - a tail read (needed anyway, because appending requires locating the end) sees only recent entries and infers the schema from whatever the most recent entries happen to do;
  - a grep/awk targeted read sees only matching lines and no header at all.
None of these is wrong under any rule currently written. L2 therefore degrades from "guaranteed" to "whatever the chosen window happened to contain", and L3 -- append rather than invent -- rests on an inference the agent cannot check. The instruction that depends on L1 remains written down and appears followed. That is precisely the shape ISS-0119 identifies: an agent can honestly report compliance having seen a third of the file.

EVIDENCE THAT L2 ALREADY FAILS IN PRACTICE, found in the file itself (this is the confirmation that this is not a theoretical risk):
  SCOPE-CHANGE appears in TWO MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE FIELD POSITIONS in the same file.
    grep -c '^  - req: SCOPE-CHANGE'   -> 31   (lines 592, 627, 671, ... 5270, 5724)
    grep -c '^    event: SCOPE-CHANGE' ->  3   (lines 3490 REQ-031, 3577 REQ-042, 3744 REQ-038, all agent: ORCH, 2026-08-17T21:48..22:15Z)
  Two readings of the same convention coexist. Neither is derivable from the header. IMPORTANT HONESTY CAVEAT, because it partially qualifies the issue's framing: the three "event: SCOPE-CHANGE" entries were written on 2026-08-17, when the file was ~3,750 lines and still WELL UNDER the read limit (3a3b236 measured 234,147 bytes). So this particular drift was NOT caused by the size limit. What it proves is stronger and slightly different from what ISS-0119 claims: the read-in-full link was already weak as a schema-transmission mechanism before it broke outright. Reading a file in full has never reliably caused an agent to notice a convention buried in one of 182 entries. The size limit did not create the weakness; it removed the last thing standing in front of it.
  Corroborating: the "event" field's own documented vocabulary has drifted too. The header documents "started | done | blocked". Actual distribution: done 107, started 54, cancelled 8, blocked 5, revised 4, SCOPE-CHANGE 3, verified 1. Three of the seven values in use are undocumented (cancelled, revised, verified), plus the malformed SCOPE-CHANGE.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: there is none to catch it. Nothing in the repo machine-validates this file (see section 3 -- zero machine-parsed referrers), the schema is enforced only by an agent's eyes, and CI has no check that the file conforms to its own header. The safeguard's only enforcement mechanism has always been the full read; there is no second line of defence.

=== 2. THE CONTRADICTION, QUOTED FROM BOTH SIDES ===

SIDE 1 -- push toward a TARGETED read. docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md:143-175, "(STOP) Load Scoped Context, Not Whole Files". Its worked example is docs/requirements.yaml, but lines 173-175 generalize explicitly and unconditionally:
  "The same rule generalizes: prefer a targeted read over a whole-file read for any file above a few hundred lines. `git diff main...HEAD` beats reading every changed file; `grep -n` beats reading a 3,000-line YAML to find one key."
  A 5,766-line YAML is squarely inside "any file above a few hundred lines", and there is no carve-out anywhere in that section for docs/status/requirement_status.yaml. Note also core-directives.md:166-167, the rationale: "the receiving agent must not have to open a 61k-token file to learn what it was asked to build."

SIDE 2 -- push toward a FULL read. Four sources, all still current:
  (i) docs/anti-patterns.md:68-83, "## Overwriting `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` instead of appending" -- "**Correct alternative:** always read the existing file in full before touching it, preserve its established schema even if a different shape seems cleaner, and append (don't replace)."
  (ii) The file's own header, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml:10 -- "# Append one entry per event. Never rewrite past entries."
  (iii) core-directives.md:328-330 -- "**3. `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` is append-only.** Read the existing file in full before touching it, preserve its established schema, append -- never rewrite."
  (iv) .claude/agents/doc-updater.md:17-18, mandatory reading -- "`docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` **in full** -- you append to it, and you must match its existing schema exactly, so a full read is genuinely required here." And :31-32 -- "read the file in full first, never guess the schema, never rewrite prior entries."

WHERE THE AGENT IS LEFT WITH NO RESOLVING RULE. The contradiction is INTERNAL TO ONE FILE, core-directives.md: line 173 says prefer targeted reads for any file above a few hundred lines; line 328, 155 lines later in the same document, says read this specific file in full. Neither references the other. Neither is scoped to exclude the other. There is no precedence rule anywhere in core-directives.md, ORCHESTRATOR.md, or HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md that says a file-specific directive overrides the general scoped-read directive, or vice versa. Sharpening it further: doc-updater.md:17-22 is the one place that resolves the tension AND IT RESOLVES IT PER-FILE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS IN ADJACENT BULLETS -- requirement_status.yaml "**in full** ... a full read is genuinely required here", then immediately requirements.yaml "**only the entries you are flipping** ... See `core-directives.md`'s 'Load Scoped Context, Not Whole Files.'" So the pipeline's answer for this file is "full read", stated deliberately and with reasons. That answer is now IMPOSSIBLE TO EXECUTE. The gap is not that the two rules conflict in the abstract -- it is that the conflict was already resolved in favour of the full read, the winning branch has become unavailable, and nothing anywhere states the fallback. The agent is left improvising at exactly the moment the safeguard is supposed to bind.

=== 3. BLAST RADIUS OF A SPLIT -- referrers RE-DERIVED, not inherited from ORCH ===

Method: grep -rn "requirement_status" across the whole repo, excluding .git/. Then each hit opened and classified. Two binary .git index matches discarded. handoffs/ and test/reports/ reported separately because they are immutable historical run artefacts, not live referrers.

(iii) MACHINE-PARSED BY CODE OR A MIX TASK: **ZERO**. Confirmed negatively, not assumed: grep -rn "docs/status" over *.ex, *.exs, *.sh, *.ps1, *.yml returns exactly two hits and BOTH ARE COMMENTS --
    mix.exs:50 -- inside the `defp aliases` block, a comment explaining why `mix letflow.check` is a mix.exs alias rather than a lib/mix/tasks task: "REQ-003's task-discovery-forces-compile problem (`docs/status/requirement_status.yaml`)". Prose citation of a historical entry; mix.exs never opens the file.
    scripts/timed_test.sh:8 -- a comment: "confirmed empirically (see docs/status/requirement_status.yaml's REQ-003 history)". The script never reads the file.
  grep -rn requirement_status .github/ returns 0. No CI job, no test, no mix task, no YAML loader touches this file. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT INPUT TO CODE-DESIGNER'S COST ESTIMATE: a split breaks no code and no gate. It is a documentation-and-agent-instruction problem only.

(ii) INSTRUCTION -- tells an agent to read, append to, or preserve the file (these MUST be updated by any split; they are the load-bearing set):
   1. CLAUDE.md:85 -- "append one event to `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` (started/done/blocked, with a real UTC timestamp...)"
   2. docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md:290 -- artifact-location table row: "| Requirement status history | `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` |"
   3. core-directives.md:328 -- the append-only + read-in-full directive quoted in section 2.
   4. core-directives.md:354 -- output-format rule: all bookkeeping is YAML "matching the format Letflow's `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` and `docs/requirements.yaml` already use."
   5. .claude/agents/doc-updater.md:17 -- mandatory reading, "**in full**".
   6. .claude/agents/doc-updater.md:23 -- pointer to the anti-patterns entry.
   7. .claude/agents/doc-updater.md:31 -- "What you do" step 2: append using the existing schema, "read the file in full first".
   8. .claude/agents/doc-updater.md:47 -- Forbidden: "Never rewrite `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` from scratch or invent a different schema".
   9. .claude/agents/release-validator.md:23 -- mandatory reading list entry.
  10. .claude/agents/release-validator.md:32 -- "not against what `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml`'s history narrates happened."
  11. docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md:46 -- DOC-UPDATER's owned-artifacts cell.
  12. docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md:105 -- "remains the append-only event history (started/done/blocked), same as before."
  13. docs/agents/AGENT_SYSTEM.md:136 -- artifact -> owner -> format table row (owner DOC-UPDATER, .yaml).
  14. docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md:129 -- names it as the naming-convention exemplar for another artefact.
  15. docs/agents/workflows/WF-01_requirement_development.md:59 -- "same append-only spirit as docs/status/requirement_status.yaml".
  16. docs/agents/workflows/WF-02_requirement_implementation.md:106 -- Step: append a `started` event.
  17. WF-02:377 -- Step Final: check it for staleness vs what shipped.
  18. WF-02:390 -- append a "done" event, "append -- do not rewrite prior entries".
  19. docs/agents/workflows/WF-04_full_test_run.md:66 -- re-verify against code "rather than what the requirement's own history in docs/status/requirement_status.yaml claims happened".
  20. docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md:156 -- "same append/never-rewrite spirit as `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml`".
  21. docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:133 -- "Record the reconciliation in `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` as a `SCOPE-CHANGE` event". SEE SECTION 4: this one is both an instruction AND the only written statement of the SCOPE-CHANGE convention, and it states it in the WRONG FIELD.
  22. docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:379 -- "see `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml`'s `SCOPE-CHANGE` entry for the full REQ-ID <-> queue-task-id mapping." An instruction to LOOK UP a specific historical entry -- a split must keep this locatable.
  23. docs/anti-patterns.md:68-83 -- the anti-pattern entry itself, including "always read the existing file in full".
  So: 23 live instruction sites across 12 files. ORCH's estimate of "roughly 13 doc referrers" UNDERCOUNTS by roughly half, mostly because several files carry 3-4 separate sites (doc-updater.md 4, core-directives.md 3, WF-02 3, AGENT_SYSTEM.md 3).

(i) PROSE MENTION ONLY -- cites the file as evidence or history; a split need not touch these except where it cites a LINE NUMBER:
  24. docs/requirements.yaml:14 (removal record), :223 (REQ-003 history), :232 (acceptance criterion text citing "requirement_status.yaml's REQ-003 history"), :275 (removal record), :444 (acceptance criterion: "a written note (in this requirement's requirement_status.yaml entry)" -- borderline instruction, it obliges a future run to write there).
  25. docs/anti-patterns.md:115, :280 -- narrative references to its events as a sequence-reconstruction source.
  26. docs/migration/stage-0-foundation.md:41, :144; stage-1-identity.md:45; stage-2-event-store-definitions.md:26; stage-3-instance-engine.md:249; decisions/0007-variable-merge-validates-new-keys.md:93.
  27. docs/status/S1-release-2026-08-16.yaml:10; docs/status/REQ-023-release-2026-08-16.yaml:218; docs/status/REQ-027-release-2026-08-16.yaml:264.
  28. docs/issues/ISS-0003:14, ISS-0008:84, ISS-0009:15, ISS-0010:54, ISS-0034:16 and :20, ISS-0037:89, ISS-0039:34 and :67, ISS-0077:91, ISS-0109:15, ISS-0119 itself.
  29. lib/letflow/design/req013-check-gate-design.md:27, :219, :226 -- design prose citing the REQ-003 saga.
  30. **lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 -- cites `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml:5158` BY LINE NUMBER.** This is the one prose referrer a split would silently falsify. There may be others of this shape; this is the only one I found. CODE-DESIGNER should treat line-number citations as a distinct hazard class.

HISTORICAL ARTEFACTS, informational, must NOT be rewritten (they are themselves append-only records): 100 files under handoffs/ mention the file; 3 files under test/reports/ (report-20260819-WF02-REQ052/053/061). A split must not retro-edit these; any renaming scheme therefore has to tolerate ~103 historical references to a path that no longer exists, or keep the original path valid.

=== 4. THE SECOND GAP -- req: SCOPE-CHANGE ===

CLAIM 1, "SCOPE-CHANGE is the established convention for work not tied to a requirement": CONFIRMED, and it is the ONLY such convention. Distribution of the `req:` field across all 182 entries: REQ-NNN 151, SCOPE-CHANGE 31, nothing else. Listing every non-REQ- value returns exactly one line: "31 SCOPE-CHANGE". Real count is 31 (ISS-0119 said "~30"; it was 30 before this run's own DOC-UPDATER entry landed in c1f5e5c, so the issue's figure was correct when written).

CLAIM 2, "there is no precedent for a `req: ISS-NNNN` entry anywhere in the file": CONFIRMED. grep -cE '^  - req: ISS-' docs/status/requirement_status.yaml -> 0. Zero, across all 182 entries. So `req: ISS-0119` for this very run would be an unprecedented invention, exactly as ISS-0119 warns.

CLAIM 3, "it is documented nowhere": **REFUTED, and the refutation makes the gap WORSE rather than better.** It IS documented in exactly one place -- docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:133-134: "Record the reconciliation in `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` as a `SCOPE-CHANGE` event, same as any other manual queue bookkeeping." But that sentence says **event**, and the 31-entry established practice puts SCOPE-CHANGE in the **req** field with a normal event value. The single written statement of the convention contradicts the overwhelming precedent -- and the file contains 3 entries (REQ-031 line 3490, REQ-042 line 3577, REQ-038 line 3744, all ORCH, all 2026-08-17) that follow the WRITTEN rule and put SCOPE-CHANGE in `event:`. So the documentation did not merely fail to record the convention; it recorded a competing one, and produced 3 divergent entries. A second, ambiguous mention at TASK_QUEUE.md:379 says "`SCOPE-CHANGE` entry" without naming a field. Neither site is in the reading list of DOC-UPDATER, the role that actually writes these entries.

WHAT THE HEADER (docs/status/requirement_status.yaml:1-17) DOES AND DOES NOT SAY. It says, verbatim:
    "# Entry shape:
     #   - req: REQ-XXX
     #     event: started | done | blocked
     #     agent: AGENT_ID
     #     at: <UTC timestamp from the clock, not memory>
     #     note: short free-text (what shipped, or what's blocking)"
  DOES say: the five field names and their order; that `req` takes the literal form REQ-XXX; that the file is history behind docs/requirements.yaml's `status:`; "Append one entry per event. Never rewrite past entries."; that `at` must come from the clock.
  DOES NOT say: anything about non-requirement work; the token SCOPE-CHANGE does not appear in the header at all; nor cancelled, revised, or verified, though all three are in active use (8/4/1 occurrences). The header's `event` vocabulary is 3 values; the file uses 7. So the header is inaccurate about BOTH the `req` field and the `event` field, and both inaccuracies are discoverable only by surveying entries -- i.e. only by the full read that no longer works.

=== 5. WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE -- constraints, NOT a chosen remedy ===

BINDING CONSTRAINTS on any design:
  C1. The append-only rule MUST NOT be relaxed. ISS-0119 states it explicitly: "Do not resolve this by relaxing the append-only rule. The rule is correct; it is the mechanism that supports it that has degraded." A design that permits rewriting, or that lowers the bar to "append carefully", fails this constraint outright.
  C2. NOTHING IN THE HISTORY MAY BE DROPPED. This file is audit trail. All 182 entries, including malformed ones, must survive byte-for-byte in content. Specifically, the 3 malformed "event: SCOPE-CHANGE" entries must NOT be silently normalized -- correcting them would be rewriting past entries and would violate C1. If the design wants them corrected, that has to be an explicit, separately-justified decision, not a side effect of a split.
  C3. C1 and C2 together imply the fix must make the safeguard EXECUTABLE, not merely restate it. Restating "read it in full" in stronger words leaves the tool refusal untouched.
  C4. Any path change must preserve resolvability of the ~103 historical references under handoffs/ and test/reports/, which cannot themselves be edited (they are append-only run records), plus the line-number citation at lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367.
  C5. Zero machine consumers exist (section 3), so no code, migration, mix task, or CI job constrains the format. This is a real degree of freedom, and CODE-DESIGNER should not spend design budget defending a format contract that nothing enforces.
  C6. The req: SCOPE-CHANGE documentation gap (section 4) is INDEPENDENT of the size problem and, per ISS-0119, "worth doing regardless of how the size problem is resolved." Any design must also reconcile TASK_QUEUE.md:133's "SCOPE-CHANGE event" wording with the 31-entry "req: SCOPE-CHANGE" practice -- otherwise the header and the protocol doc will disagree, which is how the 3 divergent entries got written in the first place.
  C7. Growth is not stopping. 181 -> 182 entries in one run; the file crossed the limit 2.5 days ago. Whatever the design is, it must have a defined behaviour at the NEXT threshold, not just clear the current one once.

WHAT EACH CANDIDATE REMEDY WOULD HAVE TO SATISFY (presented, NOT decided -- CODE-DESIGNER chooses):
  Remedy (a), split/bound the file, must additionally satisfy: an index or successor-pointer so an agent can find the current tail without knowing the split scheme; a stated rule for which shard receives the next append and what happens when it fills (C7); the 23 instruction sites in section 3(ii) updated in the same change, or they become wrong the moment the split lands; a decision on what the old path becomes so C4 holds; and a guarantee that the header/schema documentation is carried into every shard, otherwise the split multiplies the L2 problem instead of fixing it. Its advantage: it restores the literal full read, so the existing instruction text stays true. Its cost: it is the change with by far the largest documentation blast radius, and it is the only option that can break C4.
  Remedy (b), rewrite the header to prescribe an executable safeguard, must additionally satisfy: naming a CONCRETE, RUNNABLE scoped-read technique (the issue suggests "read the header block plus the last N entries") with real commands, not a principle; stating the req: SCOPE-CHANGE convention explicitly so it stops being inferred (C6); and -- critically -- it cannot live only in the file's header, because core-directives.md:328, doc-updater.md:17/31 and anti-patterns.md:68 all independently say "read in full", so those must be amended in the same change or the contradiction in section 2 survives the fix. It must also close the section-2 precedence gap by stating which of core-directives.md:173 and :328 governs this file. Its advantage: no path changes, so C4 is untouched, and it fixes the L2 weakness that predates the size limit (the 2026-08-17 drift). Its cost: it leaves C7 unaddressed -- the file keeps growing and the scoped-read window keeps covering a smaller fraction.
  Note the two are not mutually exclusive and ISS-0119 does not present them as such: it says the second is "worth doing even if the first is deferred". Both remedies independently require touching the section 2 contradiction; neither is complete without it.

NO FIX WAS IMPLEMENTED. NO REMEDY WAS CHOSEN. No file outside this handoff was modified.

issues.title: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml's header documents 3 event values (started|done|blocked) but 7 are in active use, and 3 entries put SCOPE-CHANGE in the event field instead of the req field
issues.detail: Found while diagnosing ISS-0119, reported per docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md rather than fixed here. Actual event-value distribution across the 182 entries: done 107, started 54, cancelled 8, blocked 5, revised 4, SCOPE-CHANGE 3, verified 1. The header (line 14) documents only 'started | done | blocked', so cancelled/revised/verified are undocumented conventions. Separately, three entries -- REQ-031 (line 3490), REQ-042 (line 3577), REQ-038 (line 3744), all agent ORCH, all 2026-08-17T21:48..22:15Z -- carry 'event: SCOPE-CHANGE', while 31 other entries carry 'req: SCOPE-CHANGE' with a normal event value. The divergence traces to docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:133, the only written statement of the convention, which says 'as a SCOPE-CHANGE event'.
